ags-3594-156.summary: In the spring of 1638 the Spanish ambassador at Genoa had to lay in munitions on the spot. The King had ordered the Marquis Pablo Jerónimo Pallavicino (“Palavesín”) to advance him the money; the Marquis was stalling. Velasco told the King in cipher: if he failed his suppliers, they would fail him in turn.
ags-3594-156.en:
[On the 29th of last month I reported to Your Majesty on the delays and doubts] that the Marquis Pablo Jerónimo Palavesín was raising over carrying out the royal order in which Your Majesty was pleased to command him, in the absence of ‹…›, to supply me with the money needed to lay in whatever munitions could be had here.

And now I refer to the copy of the paper with which he has answered the many requests I keep making to him to carry out Your Majesty’s royal order; for if I fail the persons with whom I had made contracts, neither will they be able to keep their engagements to me,

[in plain text:] of which it seemed right to inform Your Majesty, whose Catholic and royal person God keep as Christendom has need. Genoa, 19 May 1638. [Signature of the Count of Siruela.]

ags-3594-160.summary: A held-out cipher letter of the same ambassador, 19 May 1638, kept apart while the key was built and then read with the frozen key against its contemporary clear copy 3594,159; used only to test the key, not a reading of ours.

system: the “numerical” cipher of the Genoa embassy in 1638: vowels 16–20, syllabic series of five numbers (25 ba, 30 ca, 35 sa, 40 da, 45 la), disguised syllables (consonant changed, vowel kept: ya = ra, ha = na, at = ma), single letters (m = s, ß = n, E = t) and…
